title: Fluorine, argon, germanium, iodine and tungsten: which targets can confirm an inelastic 300-390 keV splitting?
question: For inelastic DM (m_chi = 1000 GeV, delta = 250-380 keV incl. the P007 Higgsino 366 keV), which nuclear targets can scatter at all (delta < mu v_max^2/2), what are their WimPyDD O1 rates per tonne-year relative to xenon at equal coupling, and what do PICO-60, DEAP-3600, CRESST and NaI (DAMA/LIBRA, COSINE, ANAIS) exposures imply, now and in future?
headline_result: Only nuclei with A >= 96 (delta=300 keV) to 125 (380 keV) can scatter: F, Ar, Ge, Na, Ca, O are kinematically blind at any WIMP mass, so PICO-60 C3F8 and DEAP-3600 are irrelevant; iodine gives 0.59->0.02 of the xenon rate per tonne and tungsten 16->700x (delta 300->380 keV); DAMA/LIBRA's 2.46 t yr expects 0.5 events buried in ~5e7 undiscriminated counts, CRESST <=0.04; a CaWO4 exposure of 0.68 t yr (300 keV) down to 10 kg yr (366 keV) with a ~1.2 MeV recoil window gives 3 events; published Fig. S7 inelastic limits are 500-12000x above LZ's interval
key_numbers: delta_max(1 TeV, June)=40/54/63/76/131/131/232/385/396/533 keV (C/O/F/Na/Ar/Ca/Ge/I/Xe/W); A_min=79/96/114/125 for delta=250/300/350/380; windows at 300 keV Xe 91-786, I 97-745, W 52-1255 keV; LZ ROI captures 82/45/17/2.8% of Xe window rate at 300/350/366/380; unit-coupling rates per t yr Xe 5831/209/44/8.7, I/Xe 0.59/0.30/0.14/0.023, W/Xe 16/82/222/699; best fit (c m_v^2)^2=7.4e-5 (300), 3.8e-3 (350), sigma_SI 2.2e-42/1.1e-40 cm^2; counts at best fit (300/350/366): DAMA 0.53/0.49/0.60 in 9-67 keVee vs ~5e7 bkg, CRESST-II 6e-4/6e-3/0.04, PICO CF3I 6e-4, COSINE 0.04, ANAIS 0.07, PICO C3F8 and DEAP 0; 3 events need NaI 14 t yr, CaWO4 0.68/0.073/0.0104 t yr, Xe full-window 7.0/3.8/1.5 t yr; E+(I)=745/585/516 keV, E+(W)=1255/1144/1107 keV; Fig. S7 CRESST-II/PICO above LZ upper edge 1.2e4/3.1e3 (300), 1.3e3/494 (350)
model_or_mechanism: inelastic O1 isoscalar (WimPyDD, LZ unit coupling), kinematic ceiling mu v_max^2/2 per nucleus, Baxter-2021 SHM annual/June halos, LZ one-event normalisation, recalled exposures with element mass fractions, pymupdf digitisation of Fig. S7
confidence: high (kinematic blindness map, windows) / medium (rate ratios: W Helm form factor, O1 only) / low-medium (absolute counts elsewhere: recalled exposures, unit efficiency)
